messages.content:
You are assisting with business process modelling. Decide whether a rule from a legal text is about something that the business process described below does.

INSTRUCTIONS
- First find what the rule is about: the kind of activity it deals with. Write it in law_focus, and copy the words of the passage that state it, word for word, into law_quote.
- Then look for a step in the process description where that kind of activity happens. Write that step in process_step, and copy the words of the description that state it, word for word, into description_quote.
- relevant is true if the rule is about something this process does. relevant is false if no step of the process does that kind of activity.
- This is a broad judgement. Do NOT check the rule's conditions ("if ..."), trigger events, deadlines or exceptions; they are checked in a later step. Do not mark a passage irrelevant only because a specific event or condition from the rule is not described in the process.
- Judge by what the process does, not by whether the two texts use similar words or sound like the same subject.
- Use only the two texts below. Do not assume steps that the description does not state.
- If relevant is false, process_step and description_quote are empty strings.
- reason: one sentence explaining your decision.
- Answer with one JSON object that follows the JSON schema below. Output only the JSON, with no other text.

EXAMPLE (made up, for the format only)
Rule: "If a customer complains about a card payment, the shop must refund within 14 days."
Process: "The customer chooses a product. The customer pays by card. The shop sends the product."
Answer: {"law_focus": "card payments by customers", "law_quote": "a card payment", "relevant": true, "process_step": "the customer pays by card", "description_quote": "The customer pays by card", "reason": "The rule is about card payments, and the process has a card payment step; whether a complaint happens is checked later."}

JSON SCHEMA
{
  "properties": {
    "law_focus": {
      "description": "What the rule is about: the kind of activity it deals with",
      "title": "Law Focus",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "law_quote": {
      "description": "Exact words copied from the legal passage that state what the rule is about",
      "title": "Law Quote",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "relevant": {
      "description": "true if the rule is about something this process does",
      "title": "Relevant",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "process_step": {
      "description": "The step of the process where that kind of activity happens; empty string if none",
      "title": "Process Step",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description_quote": {
      "description": "Exact words copied from the process description that state this step; empty string if none",
      "title": "Description Quote",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "reason": {
      "description": "One sentence explaining the decision",
      "title": "Reason",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "law_focus",
    "law_quote",
    "relevant",
    "process_step",
    "description_quote",
    "reason"
  ],
  "title": "RelevanceOutputV2",
  "type": "object"
}

PROCESS DESCRIPTION
This process begins when a customer signs up for a subscription service, entering personal and payment information.
The system generates an account, assigns access, and triggers automated billing cycles.
Throughout the subscription, the customer receives regular updates, product enhancements, or renewal notifications.
If the customer decides to cancel, they submit a cancellation request, which the support team processes.
Depending on the terms, any refunds or charges are applied.
The process concludes when the subscription is deactivated by the support team and the final account balance is settled.
The company is based in the Netherlands. When cancelling, many customers ask the company to remove their name, home address and card details from its systems.

LEGAL PASSAGE
[GDPR-Art17-3] General Data Protection Regulation (2016/679) - Article 17: Right to erasure (‘right to be forgotten’)
3. Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the extent that processing is necessary:
(a) for exercising the right of freedom of expression and information;
(b) for compliance with a legal obligation which requires processing by Union or Member State law to which the controller is subject or for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller;
(c) for reasons of public interest in the area of public health in accordance with points (h) and (i) of Article 9(2) as well as Article 9(3);
(d) for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with Article 89(1) in so far as the right referred to in paragraph 1 is likely to render impossible or seriously impair the achievement of the objectives of that processing; or
(e) for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.

law_focus.description: What the rule is about: the kind of activity it deals with
law_focus.title: Law Focus

law_quote.description: Exact words copied from the legal passage that state what the rule is about
law_quote.title: Law Quote

relevant.description: true if the rule is about something this process does
relevant.title: Relevant

process_step.description: The step of the process where that kind of activity happens; empty string if none
process_step.title: Process Step

description_quote.description: Exact words copied from the process description that state this step; empty string if none
description_quote.title: Description Quote

message.content: {"description_quote": "When cancelling, many customers ask the company to remove their name, home address and card details from its systems.", "law_focus": "exceptions to the right to erasure", "law_quote": "Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the extent that processing is necessary", "process_step": "customers ask the company to remove their name, home address and card details from its systems", "reason": "The rule defines exceptions to the right to erasure (data removal), and the process explicitly describes customers requesting the removal of their personal data, which is the activity the rule regulates.", "relevant": true}
